title: The welleng kick-tolerance engine: derivation, provenance and public validation against published methods
description: An open, reproducible derivation and validation of the kick-tolerance engine in welleng. The engine computes the maximum tolerable gas influx for a well design from the pore/fracture-pressure envelope, casing/hole geometry and mud weight, tracking a single migrating gas bubble to the fracture-weakest exposed point. This note is framed as reproduction and validation, not novelty or error critique: it documents what the model is built from (provenance) and shows that the implementation reproduces the worked examples of the established published methods. Validations include the single-bubble closed form of Thorogood et al. (SPE-208788-PA, 2022; intermediates digit-exact, ~1% self-contained), the kick-classification and frictional/thermal effects of Kiani Nassab et al. (SPE-202426-PA, 2022; Fig. 12 static Company-Model points), and the transitional/full-displacement kick-tolerance treatment of Santos et al. (SPE/IADC-140113-MS, 2011; SPE-159175-MS, 2012). Real-gas compressibility uses a clean-room implementation of the Hall & Yarborough (1973) Z-factor correlation, with an optional CoolProp real-EOS backend for mixtures and CO2. The engine is demonstrated end-to-end on public Equinor Volve field data (well F-13, CC BY 4.0). Every quoted validation figure is reproduced by an automated test in the welleng test suite; the Volve demonstration is reproducible via an accompanying open example script. The scope, deliberate conservatism and limitations of the single-bubble model relative to dynamic multiphase simulators are stated explicitly.
